card.title: Carry This with Me
card.instruction: Get someone to share a burden by framing participation as part of the relationship.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Help me sort our letters before the removal van comes.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You kept them. I thought you'd want the box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We filled it over ten years. I shouldn't have to decide alone what survives us.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll take the box. I just can't read them today.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then choose a day we'll open it together. Taking it away can't mean you inherit all the deciding.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 asks shared sorting, A3 makes ten years a joint deciding burden and A5 refuses to let taking the box transfer all emotional work.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 possession assumption causes A3 shared-history claim; B4 box-taking without reading causes A5 scheduled joint opening.

relationship.evidence: B2 thinks storage reflects A's preference and B4 offers responsibility while acknowledging current emotional limits.

heightening.evidence: B4 apparent relief for A is rejected as unequal in the other direction, clarifying shared participation rather than mere unloading.

specificity.evidence: A1 removal and old letters plus A3 ten years establish a relationship transition and its tangible burden.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 inheriting all the deciding gives the box transfer emotional precision; wit is restrained at 3.

coach2.inferred: People separating or moving after a long relationship.
coach2.missing: The exact legal status of the relationship is unnecessary; the shared history and deciding burden are explicit.
